title: Amazon Web Services has released Strands Box, an open-source tool that limits what AI agents may do.
key_facts: AWS has released Strands Box, open-source software that uses OS-level isolation to confine AI agents.
A policy engine, the Dogwood Local Engine, checks each tool call against earlier activity as well.
Example from AWS: an agent may post to Slack no more than three times in ten minutes.
Strands Shell and Monty for Python expose shell and Python operations to the same policy engine.
The tool is on GitHub for macOS only; Linux is in development and a Windows client is on AWS's radar with no date.
AWS VP and distinguished engineer Marc Brooker says developers remain responsible for access and human review.
quote_evidence: Strands Box supports any agent or harness one wants to confine within its walls and is available on GitHub now, though only for macOS for the time being.
Developers remain responsible for deciding what access to grant and where human review is needed
why_it_matters_hint: Companies that let AI agents act without human approval get a tool to limit them, but the limits still need people to set them well.
